music.prompt: Minimal, calm, confident instrumental score for a robotics demo film, 96 BPM. Soft low pulse and warm analog pad from the start. Around 34 seconds the music thins to almost nothing for a few seconds, then at 50 seconds a clean hopeful lift with a gentle arpeggio and light percussion. Steady and warm through the middle, a small rise near 82 seconds, resolved soft final chord at 112 seconds. No vocals. Understated, not cheesy.
music.about: The v2 score, kept: ElevenLabs had no credit left when v3 was cut (it resets on 5 December 2026). The prompt's times are v2's; the silence is placed by the edit, not the score.

numbers.about: Spoken by the voice and shown in the film's own type. The build stops unless each one is what the page said in that take AND what the checked-in files say (kaiku/policy/pretrained/study.json, baselines.json, the runner's summary).

shots.about: The swappable shot. Without --shot2 it is the hand film: the page's own camera picture beside the robot's hand, both from take hand (film/hand.py), lined up on the clock they were recorded with. With film/make.sh vN --shot2 FILE the clip fills the frame and vo_real is spoken.
shots.head: A real hand moves the robot's fingers
shots.label: Film of a real hand (it loops), played into the page as its camera
shots.label_robot: The robot's hand, same run, same moment
shots.head_real: A person's hand moves the robot's fingers

vo.text: This is film of a real hand. We play it into the page as its camera, and the robot's fingers follow it. Nothing is worn on the hand.

vo_real.text: This is a person's hand in front of a laptop camera. The robot's fingers follow the fingers. Nothing is worn on the hand.

shots.head: One robot is driven. {fleet_others} echoes redo the job, each on its own table.
shots.sub: On the live page a scripted hand drives.

vo.text: On the live page, a scripted hand drives one robot. {fleet_others_say} echoes redo the job as it happens, each on its own table.

shots.head: Kaiku off: every robot gets the same motion

vo.text: Every table is different. So if the others just copy the motion, this happens.
Same tables, Kaiku on. Each echo redoes the motion around the parts that are really there.

shots.head: What the echoes are worth: a policy trained on {study_demos} demonstrations
shots.note: Share of {study_scenes} unseen scenes sorted, mean of {study_runs} training runs. The study's demonstrations came from a scripted hand.

vo.text: Why it matters. A policy trained on {study_demos_say} demonstrations sorts {study_alone_say} of new scenes. With their echoes, {study_with_echoes_say}. {study_demos_cap} with echoes beat {study_many_say} without.

shots.about: cues: each big number appears as the voice starts to say it; then_cue the same for the line under them.

shots.head: The same {matched_demos} demonstrations, multiplied two ways
shots.note: Share of {study_scenes} unseen tables sorted, {study_runs} runs each. The replay is our own implementation, not MimicGen's code.

vo.text: Against a MimicGen-style replay, from the same {matched_demos_say} demonstrations: {matched_replay_say} with the replay, {matched_kaiku_say} with Kaiku's echoes. The replay is our own implementation.
Then nobody drives. The policy sorts scenes it has never seen.

vo.text: This is the humanoid challenge's own runner, with a mock robot. {runner_commands_say} commands went through its safety filter. None was clipped.

shots.about: The log skips from the first seconds of the run to its last second where the voice starts cut_cue; the film says how many seconds it skipped.

shots.head: Every clean run is a demonstration, in the challenge's format

vo.text: Every clean run is saved as a demonstration, in the format the challenge asks for.
It is live at {address_say}. Open it and drive it yourself.

takes.about: What is filmed. rec = a recording under WORK/../rec made with film/rec.py (or film/hand.py, film/g1log.sh); start/end are seconds into it; speed = recorded seconds per film second (everything in this cut is 1). css and init are film-only: they hide buttons, enlarge or move the page's own lines, or move the camera. They never change a word or a number. whole = filmed by one browser from start to end (close shots, where a join between two browsers shows as a twitch).

hand.about: film/hand.py's output: rec/ (the stream), inset/ + inset.jsonl (the page's camera picture, timed), hand.jsonl (what the page read and what the runner said was driving).

runner.about: Shot 8: the terminal shows WORK/g1/runner.log line by line at the moments the lines were printed. Part a starts a_from seconds into rec g1; part b starts b_lead seconds before the runner printed its summary, where the voice gets to the count.
